purpose: Synthetic conformance cases for the learning-unit validity rules of curriculum-package contract 1.2 and for the recognition of own goals through valid units (Graph Definition §13). No case represents a reviewed production learning unit.
reading: Each case lists complete landscapes in the placement-layer format. expect.findings names every finding by code; unitId and goalId are given where the finding belongs to one. expect.valid is true when findings is empty. offered and expect.offeredFindings concern the optional check against offered curricula. recognition lists learner states: explicit names the goals with an explicit result of 1, recognized the goals recognized on top of them, complete the units that are complete and unavailable the units whose completion is undefined because the unit or a required child is invalid. Only a structurally valid unit with complete reviewed coverage recognizes goals; a case with recognition states validity and reviewed coverage for each of its units in expect.units. Every explicit result counts as achieved under the current contract; the binding of results to a contract state (R5) is not part of these cases.

cases.description: Q requires B, B requires A; one unit owns all three. Valid; no reviewed coverage yet.
Year units and their primary placements are not learning units and are not validated here.
C is an own ordinary goal that no own assessment requires. It stays open and is a rule violation, never free recognition.
A is required only by the own memory goal K. Verified card recall does not prove independent application.
The only assessment that requires A belongs to another unit. A needs an own assessment of its owning unit; an assessment-only unit is a valid synthesis.
The path from Q to A runs through X of another unit and through M of another landscape. Traversal never stops at the boundary of the unit's own goals.
Q inherits the requirement of its cluster KQ on cluster KP; expansion to atoms makes Q require A and B.
Q claims coverage of C but requires only B. The missing path is a subject-review finding, not a reason for a redundant edge.
Coverage names a cluster and an unknown goal. A coverage claim names atomic goals; a cluster reference would grow with later contains changes.
A is owned by two units. Both contracts are invalid.
A landscape that declares complete coverage must own every atomic goal; clusters are never owned.
The same data with partial coverage: the open goal is counted, not rejected. An absent declaration means partial too.
A unit without own goals and without child units is an empty navigation marker, never a completed unit.
A parent with no own goals aggregates two children; its total scope is their deduplicated union. A parent with an own synthesis assessment is valid as well.
Two units name each other as parent, and a unit names itself. A further child below the cycle keeps a defined scope of its own.
A parent reference names a learning unit of the same landscape, and only a learning unit may be the child of one.
A cluster, an unknown goal and a goal of another landscape cannot be owned.
An owned goal that is both an assessment and a memory goal has no single protected role.
A genuine orientation goal may be owned; rule R1 applies to ordinary content goals only. Legacy tag encoding counts.
The normalized relation must be acyclic; a cycle through an own goal invalidates the contract.
A dangling requires reference on the path makes the contract unevaluable.
The unit declaration is closed: required wording, a dated revision, a slug ID and no field outside the contract. Learning-unit fields on another kind and a duplicated ID are rejected as well.
Ownership points at a learning unit, carries exactly goalId, unitId and relation (no context, no other field), is declared once, and a learning unit takes no other relation.
Reviewed evidence bound to the current task and rubric covers A; B has none yet. The unit is valid, its reviewed coverage incomplete.
Evidence for a changed task is stale; evidence for a goal the assessment does not claim, for a goal of no unit, or for an assessment the unit does not own is unfounded.

A coverage review has exactly its five fields, a repository-relative record and sha256 bindings; a unit has one review per assessment, and the assessment has a task, solution and rubric to bind. A review on another kind of unit is rejected.

The unit is valid on the canonical pool. Where the offered view itself targets A or B, an own assessment that requires it must be in the learning scope. A goal that is in scope only as a closure-added prerequisite demands none.
Q1 and Q2 belong to the same unit and both require A. A stays open after Q1 and is recognized once Q2 is passed as well. An explicit result never needs recognition.
Q requires B, B requires A. With only B explicitly mastered, the open Q still demands A through B. Passing Q recognizes A and B.
The open own memory goal K requires A but not B. After Q, B is recognized and A stays open until K is passed; the unit is complete only then. Assessment and memory goals are never recognized.
A, recognized under u1, stays recognized while Q2 of the later unit u2 is open, although Q2 requires A through C. Each unit recognizes only its own goals: passing Q2 alone leaves A of u1 open.
The parent p owns only the synthesis assessment QS; its required child k owns QK and A. Passing QS passes neither QK nor recognizes A. A child completed under QK stays complete while QS is open.
The orientation goal O is the entry anchor of A. While Q is open it is demanded like A; after Q both are recognized. Recognizing O asserts no motivational dialogue.
Q requires A through F, which no unit owns. An explicit result on F stops no demand: A stays demanded until Q is passed. F itself is never recognized.
